newsitem.title: USA: Transco restores pressure in Pa. gas line.
newsitem.headline: Transco restores pressure in Pa. gas line.

text.p: Transcontinental Pipe Line Co (Transco) said Thursday it was bringing pressure in its Leidy, Pa., natural gas line back to its seasonal operating level after clearing the line of debris.
The company cut pressure in the line Wednesday to clear it of parts of a dehydration unit that cluttered the line.
"The compressors are back to normal. We're back to the same levels before this happened," said Chris Stockton, referring to interruptible transportation (IT) levels.
The company would not say how much gas it was moving through the line prior to the pressure reduction. The Leidy line actually consists of several pipelines ranging in diameter from 24 to 36 inches.
Transco said earlier the problem would have no effect on its ability to meet storage commitments. The partial outage did, however, cut some IT but had no impact on firm transportation, they said.
Transco is a subsidiary of The Williams Cos Inc.
